body:
> i cannot understand why quoting is needed in that schema where no reserved key is involved.

If you turn identifier quoting on it is applied to all columns.

> If you turn identifier quoting on it is applied to all columns.

I know that.. but _WHY_ is it needed in _my specific case_? I think it is needed _ONLY_ if a column contains reserved key or some similar use case. Am i wrong? (btw it works only once, at first page load)

Also i think it is expected that once you set it to **on** all problems (_should_) go away in one shot (at cost that performance issues come in, of course).

So my thought steps was:
1. in that table there is no need of quoting -> **error**
2. ok, maybe i'am wrong in point 1 'cause i'm missing something, then i set quoting on saying bye bye to performance -> **create table sql showed**
3. good, first page loading seems ok, all happy -> _drink_
4. second time i load the page the error comes in.. so quoting is not applied or something there is not ok. -> **error**, _drink more_

Sorry if there is something stupid under my eyes i don't see or if i'm explaining it in a bad way :(

@luke83 it does not check if it is required or not, if you turn it on, it will quote all columns, not matter what. Implementing such a feature would require keeping a list of all protected words for each driver, which I have been avoiding until now.

That small discussion is not related to the error you are having, though. We could continue it elsewhere :)

@lorenzo You are right.. the main problem is "volatile quoting" take effect only first time (and solves something wrong in my schema from quoting point of view) then it is like no quoting applied and fatal error comes in.

PS: I see your point about "my schema problem", i was only asking 'cause the schema seems legitimate to me but maybe it is not :D I will do some test.. i think the problem is that **COMMENT ''**, the only one with quoting stuff.. is there a way to say "generate the schema without comment columns"? Where is the right place to ask this kind of (stupid) questions to avoid to make noise here?
What is in the schema for the comment key? Including comment '' is a bit bizzare imo. It might be an artifact of an incorrect default value that would be a simple thing to fix.

This is the CREATE sql query, generated by mysql client (heidiSql):

``` sql
CREATE TABLE `matches` (
    `id` INT(11) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    `code` VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    `home` VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    `away` VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    `homeS` INT(11) NULL DEFAULT NULL,
    `awayS` INT(11) NULL DEFAULT NULL,
    `status` CHAR(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'N',
    `created` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    `modified` DATETIME NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
    UNIQUE INDEX `code` (`code`)
)
```

this is what is generated by cakephp Table::createSql (complete code is in the issue description):

``` php
[
    (int) 0 => 'CREATE TABLE `matches` (
`id` INTEGER(11) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT COMMENT '',
`code` VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL COMMENT '',
`home` VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL COMMENT '',
`away` VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL COMMENT '',
`homeS` INTEGER(11) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '',
`awayS` INTEGER(11) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '',
`status` CHAR(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'N' COMMENT '',
`created` DATETIME NOT NULL COMMENT '',
`modified` DATETIME NOT NULL COMMENT '',
PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
UNIQUE KEY `code` (`code`)
)'
]
```

I would like to underline that the quoting feature is applied only first time the page with generation code is loaded. Then - even with `'quoteIdentifiers' => true` - only first time the code generates table sql without the fatal error. After the first load the same code will always give:

```
Error: Call to a member function quote() on a non-object    
File /home/totofriends/apps/app/vendor/cakephp/cakephp/src/Database/Driver.php  
Line: 208
```

I think it is metadata cache related because with

```
Console/cake orm_cache clear
```

and a new page load the generation is ok once. Then again fatal error since second page load.

I'm only interested to understand if it is a bug, the code it is from dummy app i'm using to test 3.0 so i'm worried about the _volatile_ behavior not about my app. Understanding why i need quoting **on** for that schema is a bonus :D (and i'm starting to thing that it is comment column related, 'cause it is the only one need a quote escape since no reserved mysql key is in place).
Matches is part of mysql's regex features, and might be the problematic bit.

body: I've fixed up the `COMMENT ''` issue in #4049.

After upgrading to last commit and after renaming table from `matches` to `games` now i got ALWAYS the error, both with quoting **on** (true) or **off** (false)

``` php
    $db = \Cake\Datasource\ConnectionManager::get('default');
    $schema = $db->schemaCollection();
    $table = $schema->describe('games');
    debug($table->createSql($db));
```

generates fatal error:

```
Fatal Error
Error: Call to a member function quote() on a non-object    
File /home/***/apps/app/vendor/cakephp/cakephp/src/Database/Driver.php  
Line: 208
```

Please forgive me if this is the expected behavior or if i'm missing something.

No that is not the expected behavior. The cited line is the attempting to use the underlying PDO connection to quote values. I'm not really sure how your driver has lost its PDO reference.

I was able to reproduce the issue locally, so I can look into the fatal error.
